title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is buzzing with activity ranging from satellite launches to defense tech investments. As nations and companies alike scramble for orbital supremacy, the challenges of space resilience and station health loom large.

themes.title: Satellite Launches Galore
themes.body: Rocket Lab's latest launch of the 10th Synspective satellite underscores the growing appetite for commercial satellite deployments. Meanwhile, Spain's backing of FOSSA highlights the increasing importance of sovereign satellite communications in a crowded orbital landscape.

themes.title: Defense Tech Investment Surge
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4B boost for space resilience signals a robust commitment to fortifying national security in orbit. Coupled with Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN program, it's clear that defense tech is attracting renewed interest from investors.

themes.title: Space Station Health Concerns
themes.body: A recent ISS repair spacewalk has raised eyebrows about the aging station's viability. As the risks mount, the international community may need to rethink its long-term plans for human presence in low Earth orbit.

themes.title: Emerging Threats in Orbit
themes.body: Russia's co-orbital activities near commercial GEO slots have drawn attention, highlighting the geopolitical tensions that are increasingly playing out in space. As Europe faces new security challenges, the need for enhanced space situational awareness becomes ever more pressing.
